subject: Post-call: LLM suitability scorecard & recommended next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@quantifyhealth.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 May 2028 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: LLM suitability scorecard & recommended next steps

Hi Samira — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and the pragmatic path I propose so we can get a short trial running next week.

1) Summary of needs we heard on the call
- Compliance sensitivity: PHI-adjacent customer support transcripts and clinical triage summaries.
- Latency SLO: 150-200ms p95 for short chat queries (<=128 tokens).
- Quality: high precision on entity extraction + concise clinical-safe responses.
- Volume: ~2M tokens/month initially; expected to double after pilot.

2) Suitability scorecard (high level)
- Open LLMs we recommend to trial: RedM-3x-q8 (cost-efficient, good NER recall), LlamaX-2.2 (strong instruction-following).
- Proprietary baseline: Quantify’s current on-prem model (we asked about their baseline perf) — baseline shows stronger few-shot summarization but costs/latency are higher.
- Gap areas: factuality on medication names, hallucination on rare procedures, and entity boundary detection.

3) Immediate next steps (recommended)
- Marissa to provide prompt bundle + benchmark harness (we have a short set ready).
- We’ll deliver a 3-day trial package: 1) baseline run on their small sample; 2) two open-model configs (quantized) with our latency/cost profile; 3) a parity checklist with acceptance thresholds.
- Schedule: propose kickoff Monday 6/3 — 30 minute alignment + provide S3 sample and credentials.

Attachments referenced: quantify_benchmarks_v1.csv (sample metrics template), prompt_bundle_v1.zip (starter prompts & negative examples).

Open questions I asked you on the call (Samira): can you share a 1k-row sample of anonymized transcripts (S3 link) and the current baseline’s p95 latency numbers? If you prefer, we can run everything inside your VPC for the trial.

Happy to jump on a quick call tomorrow to move this — what time zones work for you?

Thanks,
Jordan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[jordan@redwood.com] | +1 415-555-0192

From: Samira Khan <samira@quantifyhealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Cc: Ethan Lau <ethan@quantifyhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 30 May 2028 15:10:42 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: LLM suitability scorecard & recommended next steps

Thanks Jordan — this is helpful. A few quick clarifications: 

- We can provide a 1k-row anonymized sample by EOD Friday (I’ll share an S3 read-only link).
- Current baseline latency: our on-prem model is ~320ms p95 for 128-token prompts (including pre/post processing).
- Acceptance threshold: our product team would be comfortable if an open model meets >=95% of baseline precision on our NER test and latency <= 200ms p95. Is that realistic?

Also — we have strict logging/retention rules. For the trial, can we run in a private mode where logs aren’t persisted by Redwood beyond the short window for analysis?

Samira
VP Product | Quantify Health
samira@quantifyhealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@quantifyhealth.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 31 May 2028 09:05:18 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: LLM suitability scorecard & recommended next steps

Hi Samira — quick tech notes and what we’ll include in the prompt/benchmark bundle.

On acceptance: the criteria you suggested (>=95% baseline precision on NER and <=200ms p95) are strict but achievable on a subset of intents with targeted prompt engineering + light instruction tuning. We’ll flag where we expect regressions.

What we’ll deliver in the trial bundle (attachments included):
- prompt_bundle_v1.zip — initial few-shot templates, negative examples, and a short instruction-tuning recipe.
- quantify_benchmarks_v1.csv — CSV with columns: uid, gold_entities, baseline_pred, open_modelA_pred, open_modelB_pred, latency_ms, notes.
- harness/driver — a small script we’ll run (or handoff) to compute the parity metrics and produce a failure-rate by entity type.

Benchmarks we suggest (links included in Drive):
- NER precision/recall curve by entity type (PHI vs clinical terms).
- Hallucination checks using 200 adversarial prompts (we’ll include examples).
- Latency profiles at 1, 5, 20 RPS for 64/128-token requests.

Privacy modes: we can run the trial inside your VPC (we’ll provide a private agent image) so no logs leave your environment. If that’s not possible for the first pass, we have a short-retention mode (24 hrs) with explicit deletion callbacks and audit logs.

I’ve attached the initial CSV and prompt bundle stub. If you’d like, Jordan and I can build a small acceptance dashboard that shows per-entity delta vs your baseline.

—Marissa
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments: quantify_benchmarks_v1.csv (attachment), prompt_bundle_v1.zip (attachment)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@quantifyhealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 31 May 2028 10:02:50 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: LLM suitability scorecard & recommended next steps

Thanks Marissa — and thanks Samira for confirming the baseline numbers. Action items and timeline below: 

Action owner + ETA:
- Samira: share S3 read-only sample link — ETA: Fri 5/31 EOD (you said you could).
- Marissa: run the sample through the harness against the proprietary baseline and two open configs (RedM-3x-q8, LlamaX-2.2) — ETA: Mon 6/3 close of day. Outputs: populated quantify_benchmarks_v1.csv + short summary.
- Jordan: schedule a 30-minute kickoff 6/3 10:00am PT (calendar invite sent) to confirm run parameters and acceptance gates.
- Soojin: prepare parity checklist and SOW draft for a short pilot (I dropped a rough SOW into Drive).

Acceptance thresholds (proposed, please confirm):
- NER precision: >=95% of baseline on high-priority entities (medication, dosage, condition).
- Latency: <=200ms p95 for 128-token prompts on dedicated trial capacity.
- Hallucination failure rate: <3% on adversarial set for clinical facts.

If the open models meet these gates on the pilot dataset, we’ll propose a 6-week pilot (DEAL-9876) with routing rules and cost/latency profiles for production rollout. If they don’t, we’ll capture the regression signals and propose mitigations (instruction tuning, lightweight adapter fine-tune, or hybrid routing back to baseline for failing intents).

Samira — confirm S3 link and your preference on private VPC vs short-retention. Once we have the sample, Marissa will run the harness and we’ll share a first-pass readout within 48 hours.

Thanks,
Jordan

From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 02 Jun 2028 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: acceptance thresholds & parity notes (internal)

Jordan/Marissa — internal alignment notes (posting here so we have a single source of truth before the kickoff). This message is internal only; please don’t forward verbatim to Quantify.

- We should avoid using the word “replace” in external comms; focus on "complement" and "parity gates".
- For the parity checklist: include entity-level delta table, a small confusion-matrix export for top 10 entities, and a risk flag for hallucination-sensitive intents.
- Cost/latency table: show 3 scenarios (hosted open model, dedicated open model, fallback to baseline) with per-token $ and estimated monthly bill for their 2M->4M tokens.
- If an open model meets NER precision but fails hallucination gates, propose a targeted adapter fine-tune (2-4 days) as the next experiment before recommending full cutover.
- SOW: short pilot (6 weeks), success criteria are the three acceptance thresholds Jordan proposed; include an explicit "fallback" SLA if degradation is detected (route to baseline within 5 minutes of regression alert).

I’ve dropped a SOW draft in Drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=sow_draft_20280531. I also added a HubSpot note under DEAL-9876.

—Soojin
Head of Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
